chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal narrated from Ali ibn Ya'qub al-Hashimi from Marwan ibn Muslim from Hariz from Burayd, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying: 'A man entrusted me with wealth, then he died, and his children have nothing, and he did not perform the Hajj of Islam.' He said: 'Perform Hajj on his behalf, and if anything remains, give it to them.'

key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَامِ: the Hajj of Islam (the first obligatory Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What happens to a deceased person's entrusted wealth if they died without performing Hajj and their heirs are poor?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the priority of fulfilling the deceased's obligatory Hajj using entrusted funds before distributing any remainder to heirs, highlighting the spiritual debt's precedence over worldly inheritance. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the *Hajjat al-Islam* (the first Hajj) is a personal obligation that must be discharged from the estate, even if it requires utilizing assets held in trust, provided the heirs' rights are preserved from any surplus.
